description: The repository-level commitMessagePrefix is for the config-migration pull request, which is no package update and so is reached by no packageRule: without it Renovate hard-codes the scope `config` into that header.

Nothing this repository pins reaches a consumer: every tracked version is CI, lint or release tooling, and the skills pin nothing. So every update is `chore`, which release-please hides, on an internal scope. The shared presets type updates feat or fix by semver level on an empty scope and add '!' to majors; either would cut a release, the '!' a major one.

The type and scope are claimed for every update carrying a package name, with no matchUpdateTypes for an unnamed update type to fall through. The prefix is restated without '!'. All three sit after the presets, so a preset pin bump cannot change the header shape.

packageRules.description: A `uses:` ref keeps its own scope, claimed here so the header does not depend on an upstream matcher.
A shared-preset pin decides how every other update is typed and scoped, so its bump takes the scope of the configuration it lives in.

Renovate's package-name matcher never matches an upgrade that carries no package name, so the first rule cannot reach a lockfile refresh. Matched by update type so it holds for any manager that grows a lockfile.

Everything under .mise/locks/ is generated by `mise lock` from the pins in mise.toml, which the mise manager already tracks. Left enabled, the npm and pep621 managers update these files directly: a second update for the same tool, out of step with mise.lock.
